svg.aria-label: B1-01 — the diagnostic: a flat derivative is what infinite-acting radial flow looks like
svg.desc: Log-log diagnostic plot for the synthetic B1 drawdown. The upper curve is the pressure drop, rising steadily from about 337.7 to 409.4 psi across the window. The lower curve is the Bourdet derivative with respect to natural-log time, which is flat across the whole window at close to 18.5325 psi, the value 70.6 q B mu / k h takes at the declared properties. A dashed rule marks that ideal plateau. The derivative sits just below the rule everywhere, by at most 0.000657 percent, which is the known 1/(8 t_D) deficit of the line-source solution and not an error. Full values in the data table below.

svg.text: Synthetic drawdown and its Bourdet derivative, both on logarithmic axes, over t_D from 3.32e+4 to 1.59e+6. The derivative is flat because the response

svg.text: is a straight line on a semilog plot, which is the definition of the regime. Smoothing L = 0.1.

svg.text: The derivative is deliberately compared against (1/2)exp(-1/(4 t_D)) rather than against the round 1/2. The deficit from 1/2 is a real feature of the

text.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, "Noto Sans", sans-serif, "Apple Color Emoji", "Segoe UI Emoji"

svg.text: line-source solution, worth 0.000657 percent here, and testing against 1/2 would hide that systematic difference inside whatever tolerance was

svg.text: generous enough to pass. Measured against the closed form the worst error is 2.09e-8 relative.

svg.text: A flat derivative identifies the regime; it does not identify the reservoir. Any model that produces radial flow over this window would look the same here,

text.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, "Noto Sans", sans-serif, "Apple Color Emoji", "Segoe UI Emoji"

svg.text: which is why B1 claims nothing beyond the model it declares.
